Requirement: "invoke host Python with -I and a sanitized import path" (security audit recommendation in issue #6308)
Expected change site: every `python3 -` and `python3 -c` invocation executed by the `codex-agent` job across the support scripts the workflow stages (review_apply_fixes.sh, review_consolidate.sh, review_run_reviewers.sh, review_collect_pr_metadata.sh, review_commit_changes.sh, review_agents_md_materiality.sh, review_reject_verify.sh, review_filter_uninteresting_files.sh, workspace_safety_check.sh, write_guard.sh, codex_stall_guard.sh, codex_heartbeat.sh, pr_checks_lib.sh, review_conflict_prepare.sh, review_single_issue_security_pass.sh, and others)
Evidence of absence: the PR diff only adds the `-I -B` defense-in-depth to the two stdin invocations in `scripts/workspace_init.sh` (lines 126 and 272). All other `python3 -` / `python3 -c` invocations across the review pipeline retain only the job-level `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`, which is silently ignored on Python < 3.11 — the workflow does not pin a Python version (no `setup-python` step, no version check), so on any runner with an older interpreter the PR-controlled `sitecustomize.py` / `pathlib.py` / `shutil.py` shadow remains effective for those invocations. The new test `test_bootstrap_sibling_imports_survive_safe_path` (tests/test_review_host_python_safe_path.py:103-110) is gated behind `skipif sys.version_info < (3, 11)`, so the protection is not even verified on the older-Python path the audit warning covers. The `agents.md` note acknowledges the 3.11 floor but does not address the broader coverage gap. Per the issue's recommendation, the hardening should apply to every host-Python invocation the credential-bearing job starts, not just the two in `workspace_init.sh`.
